title: Marketplace listing value-prop playbook and preflight
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact playbook and preflight checklist focused on value-prop messaging, technical listing requirements, and launch readiness for cloud marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure) listings and partner co-publishes. Use this as the canonical draft for copy variants, acceptance criteria, and the minimum asset set required to avoid repeat back-and-forths with marketplace teams.

Audience:
- GTM launch PMs and content writers
- Partner managers and integrations engineers
- Legal/finance reviewers for SKU mapping and contract language

TL;DR (one-sentence):
Ship a concise listing that highlights predictable inference economics (latency, cost controls, private + hosted modes), includes 3 ready UX copy variants for marketplace cards, and passes the 10-point technical & compliance preflight below.

High-level positioning (for all marketplace variants):
- Headline theme: "Production-ready LLM inference that scales — hosted, dedicated, or private."
- Core bullets to surface in marketplace bullets (3 items):
  1) Predictable performance (SLA-backed latency tiers and dedicated pools)
  2) Cost controls + Optimize toolkit (batching, KV cache, quantization suggestions)
  3) Enterprise-ready options (VPC/private control plane, KMS/HSM integrations)

Persona-driven short copy snippets (for A/B testing):
- For Platform Engineers (technical): "Reduce per-token cost and tail latency with a GPU-optimized serving runtime — supports quantized model variants, automatic KV caching, and can be deployed to your VPC."
- For Product/Feature owners: "Ship LLM features fast with predictable costs and built-in quality monitoring — try hosted API then scale to dedicated capacity when you need predictability."
- For Security/Compliance buyers: "Private deployments and on-prem options with audit logs, KMS support, and SOC/ISO-ready controls."

Marketplace card variations (ready-to-drop):
- Short headline (<= 60 chars): "Low-latency LLM inference — hosted & private"
- One-line subhead: "Scale production LLMs with predictable cost, SLAs, and VPC-ready deployments."
- 2-sentence description (marketplace long summary): "Redwood Inference delivers production-grade LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Developers get a single API for generation, embeddings, streaming, and function calls — plus tooling to optimize batching, caching, and model variants for cost and latency."

SEO/meta description (140 chars):
"High-performance LLM inference: hosted API, dedicated GPU pools, and private VPC deployments with cost & latency controls."

CTA variants to include in asset package:
- Primary CTA: "Get started — free trial credits"
- Secondary CTA: "Request enterprise demo"
- Tertiary (security-focused): "Ask about private deployment"

Technical preflight checklist (must clear before submission):
1) Asset file formats: PNG (1200x627) hero image, SVG logo (transparent), 3x screenshots (console model route, cost breakdown, rollout UI).
2) Short copy: headline, subhead, 250-char summary, 1000-char long description.
3) Integration docs link (public or partner limited): install guide + quickstart (must include sample curl and SDK snippet).
4) Pricing/SKU mapping: one line for hosted (usage per token), one for dedicated (monthly commit), one for private (license + support).
5) Contact routing: email redirect or partner form to track inbound leads (set UTM and marketplace source tag).
6) Marketplace technical test user: staging account and API key for vetting (expiration + notes).
7) Legal: approved short terms blurb + refund/credits policy for marketplace purchases.
8) SLAs: clearly state latency/uptime SLA tiers or link to SLA PDF.
9) Compliance: checklist for regions supported, data residency, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS support.
10) Accessibility & localization plan: primary EN-US copy and list of target locales for launch.

Acceptance criteria (what product/ops must verify):
- All assets match marketplace image/type specs and are accessible via public CDN or partner asset ID.
- Quickstart runs end-to-end with sample model call in under 2 minutes for reviewers.
- Pricing is expressed in marketplace SKU format and reconciles with billing team mapping (include mapping doc id).
- Lead routing is confirmed to CRM (HubSpot/SFDC) test endpoint and UTM params preserved.

SKU/pricing mapping (draft recommendations):
- Hosted API: usage-based tokens (tier 1: $0.0008 / token unit for up to 50M tokens / mo, tier 2: discounted commit).
- Dedicated: reserved cluster (monthly commit, profile by vGPU hours — example: dedicated-4xA100-monthly = $X/month).
- Private: platform license + deployment support band (license + professional services estimated in quote).

Smoke test scenarios for marketplace reviews (QA):
- New customer signs up via marketplace -> receives trial credits -> calls generate endpoint -> receives streaming response without errors.
- Request falls back to compatible model variant when capacity limited (simulate capacity throttle).
- Billing event triggered after usage threshold; invoice/test SKU reconciles with mock billing.

Common rejection reasons and mitigation notes (learned from past listings):
- Missing or low-resolution imagery: always include high-res hero and console screenshots.
- Unclear pricing mapping: include explicit SKU codes and link to finance mapping doc.
- No vetting token for technical review: generate a time-limited demo key with clear scope.
- Security questions unanswered: prepare short one-page on encryption & logging.

Launch sequence (recommended):
1) Internal content freeze (writers + legal sign-off) -> 2) Marketplace submission (include staging access) -> 3) Marketplace QA cycle (2–5 business days typical) -> 4) Public publish + partner announcement -> 5) First-week analytics review and content tweaks.

Metrics to monitor in first 30 days:
- Listing impressions and click-through rate (CTR).
- Trial sign-ups via marketplace (conversion rate).
- API onboarding time (median time from sign-up to first successful API call).
- Early churn signals from billing mismatch or onboarding friction.

Open questions (to resolve in next sync):
- Do we want separate listing pages per cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure) or a single multi-cloud asset? Tradeoffs: more review cycles vs cloud-specific marketplace SEO.
- Final pricing bands for dedicated cluster types (need finance input).
- Whether to include a short video demo (30–60s) in the listing — ask creative if V1 is feasible in 2 weeks.

Next steps & owners (60-day runway):
- Content: finalize 3 card copy variants and meta descriptions (Owner: Ava Chen, due 2025-02-10).
- Engineering: produce staging review key and quickstart snippet with cloud-region example (Owner: Miguel Torres, due 2025-02-14).
- Legal/Finance: finalize SKU mapping & marketplace terms blurb (Owner: Priya Nair, due 2025-02-18).
- Partner ops: confirm lead routing to CRM and test lead workflow (Owner: Samir Patel, due 2025-02-21).

Quick reference copy snippets (pick one for marketplace long description):
- Version A (developer-first): "Redwood Inference: a high-throughput runtime and orchestration for running LLM workloads in production. Choose hosted API for fast iteration, dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, or a private deployment for regulated workloads. Built-in batching, KV caching, and model lifecycle tools reduce cost without sacrificing quality."
- Version B (value-first): "Cut inference cost and tail-latency with a serving runtime tuned for production. Redwood helps engineering teams ship LLM features quickly and operate them at scale — across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."

Notes to reviewer:
- This doc should be treated as an opinionated starting point — replace placeholder pricing with finance-signed values before publish.
- Keep copy punchy on the marketplace card; use the long description for detail.

Unresolved: list of asset file names and final hero image selection (do not block submission if alternative hero provided; mark it as contingent asset).

End of playbook.
